questions.q: At which value of $p$ is the Bernoulli variance largest?
options: It is the same for every $p$
questions.explain: $p(1-p)$ peaks at $p = 0.5$ with value $0.25$ — maximum uncertainty. At $p = 0$ or $p = 1$ the outcome is certain and the variance is $0$.

questions.q: Using $P(X = x) = p^x (1-p)^{1-x}$ for $x \in \{0, 1\}$, what is $P(X = 0)$ when $p = 0.8$?
questions.explain: With $x = 0$: $p^0 (1-p)^1 = 1 - p = 0.2$. The formula is just a compact way of writing $P(X=1) = p$ and $P(X=0) = 1-p$.

questions.q: Dropout drops each neuron with rate $r = 0.5$ during training. How does the page model this?
options: As one Binomial draw for the whole network
As a Normal random variable added to each weight
As an independent Bernoulli($r$) on/off switch per neuron
As a deterministic rule that drops every other neuron
questions.explain: Each neuron gets its own two-outcome random switch — a Bernoulli trial with parameter $r$ (not the coin's $p$). Summing many such switches would give a Binomial count.
